articles.title: Risk stratification in conservatively treated pediatric lateral humeral condyle fractures: the prognostic value of articular gap and initial displacement - a retrospective cohort study.
articles.population: Children with lateral humeral condyle fractures treated without surgery
articles.outcomes: Radiographic union, displacement progression, time to union, and complications
articles.take_home: Most minimally displaced lateral humeral condyle fractures in children heal well without surgery, but those with a gap at the fracture line or initial displacement of 2 mm or more are at higher risk of the fracture shifting, taking longer to heal, and developing complications.

articles.title: Establishing the UK clubfoot research priorities : a multiple-stakeholder consensus study.
articles.authors: Trees A, Baird EJ, Lockey D, Douglas C, Ashby E, Campbell DM, et al.
articles.study_type: Consensus study using modified Delphi technique
articles.population: UK stakeholders in clubfoot management including healthcare professionals, patients and carers
articles.sample_size: 103 participants in round one, 93 in round two
articles.outcomes: Nine research priorities identified across four themes: Primary Treatment, Bracing, Relapse, and Physiotherapy
articles.take_home: Healthcare professionals and patients agreed that the most important areas for future clubfoot research are preventing relapse and optimising bracing, particularly understanding whether using a brace on one foot or both feet works better. This consensus will help guide future clinical trials to improve clubfoot treatment.

articles.title: Pediatric Nonscaphoid Carpal Fractures: Fracture Distribution and Operative Management in an Institutional Cohort and 2 National EHR Databases.
articles.authors: Flood MG, Rice S, Khan A, Walsh H, Garcia-Owusu A, Tanner N, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective cohort study using institutional database and 2 national electronic health record databases
articles.population: Children and adolescents under 18 years old with nonscaphoid carpal fractures
articles.sample_size: 48 patients at institutional centre; 4464 in TriNetX database; 2126 in Epic Cosmos database
articles.outcomes: Fracture distribution by type, demographic patterns, rates of operative versus non-operative management, and complications
articles.take_home: Nonscaphoid carpal fractures in children are rare injuries that usually affect adolescent boys, with triquetrum being the most common type and hamate fractures most likely to need surgery. The vast majority of these fractures are treated without an operation.

articles.title: Osteosynthesis With Barrel-Bone Grafting Technique for Failed Recalcitrant Cases of Congenital Pseudarthrosis of Tibia: Outcomes and Complications in a Series of 17 Patients.
articles.authors: Agashe MV, Iyer NV, Shekhawat YS, Vaidya SV
articles.population: Children with congenital pseudarthrosis of the tibia who had failed previous surgery
articles.outcomes: All 17 patients achieved bone union at mean 4 months. No refractures occurred during follow-up (mean 27 months). Two patients achieved cross-union, 3 achieved 3-in-1 union, and 12 had tibial union. Mean leg-length difference was 2.3 cm. Minor complications included 1 superficial skin necrosis, 1 delayed wound healing, and 3 cases of ankle valgus.
articles.take_home: The barrel-bone grafting technique successfully healed this difficult bone condition in all 17 children, with no bones re-breaking during follow-up. This method appears to be an effective option for children whose previous surgery did not work.

articles.title: Comparison of the modified Brostrom-Gould procedure for chronic lateral ankle instability in adolescents with and without an os subfibulare : a propensity score-matched study.
articles.authors: Xiong S, Li Y, Liu Z, Zhao F, Jiang D, Hu Y, et al.
articles.study_type: Retrospective comparative study with propensity score matching
articles.population: Adolescent patients with chronic lateral ankle instability undergoing modified Brostrom-Gould procedure
articles.sample_size: 82 matched patients (41 with os subfibulare, 41 without)
articles.outcomes: Patient-reported pain and function scores (VAS, Karlsson score, Tegner score, FAOS), re-sprain rates, return to sport time, satisfaction, and complications
articles.take_home: Adolescents with chronic ankle instability had good outcomes from surgery regardless of whether they had an os subfibulare. Those with high sporting demands or certain types of ligament injury had a higher chance of the ankle giving way again after surgery.

articles.title: Surgical management of unstable juvenile osteochondritis dissecans of the knee: clinical outcomes, return to sport, complications, and reoperation rates with an average follow-up of 6.5 years.
articles.authors: Carabajal Mattar M, Kohan Fortuna Figueira S, Marangoni L, Costa Paz M, Molina Romoli A, Astoul J, et al.
articles.population: Children and young people with unstable osteochondritis dissecans of the knee
articles.outcomes: Clinical outcomes, return to sport, complications, and reoperation rates
articles.take_home: The study followed young patients who had surgery for unstable knee osteochondritis dissecans over an average of 6.5 years to understand how well they recovered and whether they could return to sport.

articles.title: Surgical outcomes for displaced lateral humeral condyle fractures in children: a retrospective study comparing two types of tension band wiring procedures and pinning.
articles.authors: Yano K, Kawabata A, Adachi T, Ohki K, Kaneshiro Y, Yokoi T, et al.
articles.population: Children with displaced lateral humeral condyle fractures
articles.sample_size: 63 patients (24 buried tension band wiring, 24 nonburied wires with buried suture, 15 pinning)
articles.outcomes: Bony union rates, range of elbow motion, Flynn criteria for function and cosmesis, number of operations under general anaesthesia, delayed union, surgical site infection
articles.take_home: All three surgical techniques produced equivalent clinical results with good bone healing and elbow function. Buried tension band wiring had fewer complications like delayed healing and infection, though it required a second operation to remove the wires.

articles.title: Finding the physeal midpoint for distal femoral hemiepiphysiodesis utilizing novel anatomic measurements.
articles.authors: Johnson BT, Khalil AZ, Froerer DL, Metz AK, Hughes IX, Matter AL, et al.
articles.study_type: Diagnostic accuracy study using computed tomography imaging
articles.population: Paediatric patients undergoing assessment for distal femoral hemiepiphysiodesis
articles.outcomes: Accuracy and reliability of three radiographic landmarks for identifying the distal femoral physeal midpoint: diaphyseal midpoint, apex of physeal undulation, and inferior point of Blumensaat's line
articles.take_home: The inferior point of Blumensaat's line is the most accurate and reliable radiographic landmark for finding where to place hardware during minimally invasive surgery to correct knee deformities in children. Using this landmark during surgery may help surgeons position hardware more precisely.

articles.title: Management trends and outcomes of femur fractures in children with cerebral palsy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
articles.authors: Garabedian M, Benaroch LR, Charron B, Alatassi R, Carey T, Bartley D, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 0-18 years with cerebral palsy who had femur fractures
articles.sample_size: 258 patients with 335 femur fractures across 7 included studies
articles.outcomes: Fracture location, ambulatory status, treatment types, malunion rates, and complications including pressure sores, pneumonia and surgical site infection
articles.take_home: Most femur fractures in children with cerebral palsy occurred in the distal femur and were treated without surgery in non-walking children, though this approach had higher complication rates. Surgery was preferred for certain fracture types and ambulatory children, with better healing outcomes but some surgical risks like infection.

articles.title: Pelvic fixation in pediatric spinal fusion for neuromuscular scoliosis is associated with increased short-term complications but comparable long-term outcomes.
articles.authors: Meydan Y, Sacks GI, Lebens RS, Barsi JM
articles.population: Paediatric patients aged 21 years or under with neuromuscular scoliosis undergoing posterior spinal fusion
articles.sample_size: 592 matched pairs (985 with pelvic fixation and 1492 without, before matching)
articles.outcomes: Short-term complications (1-365 days) including infections and wound breakdown; long-term complications (365+ days) including pseudoarthrosis, revision surgery and additional instrumentation; mortality
articles.take_home: Children with neuromuscular scoliosis who have pelvic fixation during spinal fusion surgery have more wound infections and healing problems in the first year after surgery. However, the long-term results are similar between those who have pelvic fixation and those who do not.

articles.title: The Relationship Between Screw Placement and Southwick Angle Remodeling in Slipped Capital Femoral Epiphysis.
articles.authors: Tomaru Y, Saisu T, Kamegaya M, Tsuruoka H, Tsukagoshi Y, Nozawa D, et al.
articles.population: Children and young people with slipped capital femoral epiphysis treated with in situ pinning
articles.outcomes: Change in Southwick angle (a measure of femoral head positioning) from immediately after surgery to 1 year follow-up, and association with screw placement position
articles.take_home: The femoral head position improved on average over the first year after surgery, with anterior screw placement associated with slightly more improvement, but the researchers recommend central screw placement for safety rather than trying to position screws anteriorly for marginal gains.

articles.title: Telescopic rods vs. non-telescopic rods in the treatment of osteogenesis imperfecta: A systematic review.
articles.authors: Yoshida R, Sombra MP, Cardoso MO, Nogueira MP
articles.outcomes: Revision rates and complication rates between telescopic and non-telescopic intramedullary rods
articles.take_home: Telescopic rods had significantly lower revision rates than non-telescopic rods in children with osteogenesis imperfecta, with no difference in overall complication rates. This suggests telescopic rods may be preferable as they reduce the need for repeat operations.

articles.title: Phase 3 Trial of Oral Infigratinib in Children with Achondroplasia.
articles.authors: Savarirayan R, Hoover-Fong J, Irving M, Arundel P, de Bergua JM, Campeau PM, et al.
articles.population: Children aged 3 to 17 years with achondroplasia
articles.outcomes: Primary: annualized height velocity at 52 weeks. Secondary: height z score and upper-to-lower body segment ratio at 52 weeks. Adverse events monitored throughout.
articles.take_home: Infigratinib increased children's growth rate by approximately 1.74 cm per year more than placebo, with comparable safety profiles between treatment and placebo groups over 52 weeks.
